_about: What each check stands on, in the order it is looked for: the editor's documentation, public reports, a local test. A level left out is not claimed. Measured precision is in precision.json.

tested.result: With block: the call was refused, "PreToolUse:Bash hook error: [node .../missing-check.js]: failed; blocking because onFailure is \"block\"". Without: `ls` ran. The no-effect cases (Stop, async) were not tested.

tested_skill_hooks_empty.how: claude -p --model haiku --setting-sources project --output-format stream-json --verbose --no-session-persistence --strict-mcp-config --allowedTools Skill, from an empty temporary git repository holding .claude/skills/shop-orders/SKILL.md (frontmatter name, description, `hooks: []`; body: reply with a marker word) and a control skill without `hooks`; asked to call the Skill tool with shop-orders and reply what it says. 35-hooks-matcher.documented: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks (Matcher patterns: only letters, digits, _, -, spaces, `,` and `|` make an exact list; any other character makes the whole matcher one JavaScript regular expression on the tool name; argument patterns go in `if`)
35-hooks-matcher.documented_note: Scope of this entry: a permission rule written as one `|` alternative of a matcher (NOTICE when the matcher is a valid regular expression, ERROR when it is not). The page does not say what an invalid regular expression does; that part is measured only.

tested.how: claude -p --model haiku --setting-sources project --output-format stream-json --verbose --no-session-persistence --strict-mcp-config --allowedTools Bash Write, in two empty temporary git repositories. Each .claude/settings.json has two PreToolUse command hooks that append the hook input's tool_name to a log in the repository: the probed matcher, and a control matcher `Bash|Write`. Probed matchers: `Bash(git *)|Write` (a valid regular expression), `Write|Edit(*.ts)` (not one). Asked to run `git status` with Bash, then create note.txt with Write. One run each. Replayed by probes/run_probes.py.
tested.result: `Bash(git *)|Write`: fired on Write only, not on the `git status` Bash call. `Write|Edit(*.ts)`: fired on nothing. The control fired on Bash and Write in both repositories, so an invalid matcher does not stop the other groups of the same event.

frontmatter-bom.documented_note: Not an audit.py check of its own: the frontmatter readers used by 02-skill-frontmatter, 08-agent-frontmatter, 19-frontmatter-quoting, 22-rule-glob-match and the frontmatter hooks of 35-hooks-shape skip a UTF-8 byte order mark before the opening `---` since 0.26.0. The skills, sub-agents and memory pages were not found to mention a byte order mark (audit relecture, 2026-10-17); not re-read for this entry.

tested.how: claude -p --model haiku --setting-sources project --output-format stream-json --verbose --no-session-persistence --strict-mcp-config --allowedTools Read, from an empty temporary git repository. Files opening with a byte order mark, each beside a twin without one: skill shop-refunds (description with a marker word, body with another), skill shop-coupons with `user-invocable: false` (twin shop-discounts), agent file shop-reviewer.md with frontmatter name shop-reviewer-bom (twin shop-tester-plain), rule payments.md with paths src/payments/** (twin web.md with src/web/**), plus an unconditional rule and an InstructionsLoaded command hook logging file_path and load_reason. Asked to Read src/web/page.ts, then src/payments/amount.ts, then quote the description of shop-refunds from its skills listing without another tool. Read from the stream: init.skills, init.agents, tool_use; from the hook log: each load. One run. Replayed by probes/run_probes.py (--only frontmatter-bom).
tested.result: Skill with a mark: in init.skills, and the reply quoted its frontmatter description exactly, marker included, without the body's marker and without reading the file (the model's own account). Skill with a mark and `user-invocable: false`: left out of init.skills, as its twin without a mark: the field was read. Agent with a mark: in init.agents under its frontmatter name. Rule with a mark: loaded only on reading src/payments/amount.ts (load_reason path_glob_match), not at session start, like its twin on src/web/page.ts; the unconditional rule and CLAUDE.md loaded at session_start. Side observation, not used as a signal: `disable-model-invocation: true` left a skill in init.skills, with or without a mark.

01-claude-md-import-syntax.documented: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory.md (Import additional files: "Relative paths resolve relative to the file containing the import, not the working directory. Imported files can recursively import other files, with a maximum depth of four hops."; "Without the backslashes, the path ends at the first space"; "A path wrapped in quotes isn't imported at all"; "Import parsing skips Markdown code spans and fenced code blocks.")
01-claude-md-import-syntax.documented_note: Read 2026-10-17. Scope: what the auditor counts as an `@path` import (parsing/markdown.py import_tokens), shared by 17-always-loaded-budget, 01-claude-md-import (now on every file of the import walk, repo.walk_imports) and the NOTICE 01-claude-md-import-syntax. The page does not say what punctuation next to a path does; that part is measured only.

tested.how: claude -p 'Reply with the single word OK.' --model haiku --setting-sources project --output-format stream-json --verbose --no-session-persistence --strict-mcp-config, from an empty temporary git repository whose .claude/settings.json has an InstructionsLoaded command hook appending each event (file_path, load_reason) to a log. CLAUDE.md holds one paragraph per form, each naming its own file under docs/ (all files exist): `@docs/space.md` followed by a space; at a line end; at the end of the file with no newline; followed by `:`, `,`, `.`, `"`, `;`, `!`, `?`, `)`; `@docs/colonfile.md:` and `@docs/commafile.md,` beside files literally named `docs/colonfile.md:` and `docs/commafile.md,`; preceded by `(`, `"`, `'`, a lone backtick, a word character (`shop@docs/...`); wrapped in double quotes; in a code span; in a fenced block; `@./docs/dotrel.md`; `@docs/slash.md/` (a file, trailing slash); `@docs/folder/` (a folder holding inner.md); `@docs/NOTES` (no extension). Plus a chain CLAUDE.md -> docs/h1.md -> h2 -> ... -> h6, each written relative to the importing file (`@h2.md` inside docs/h1.md), and in docs/h1.md `@docs/rootrel.md`, a file that exists only relative to the repository root. One run, cost $0.0018. `@~/` was not probed (it would read the home folder). An earlier run the same day (same flags, one run) had loaded only `@docs/plain.md` out of `@docs/plain.md`, `@docs/colon.md:`, `@docs/comma.md,`, `@docs/period.md.` and `(@docs/paren.md)`. Replayed by probes/run_probes.py (--only 01-claude-md-import-syntax).
tested.result: Loaded (load_reason include): space after, line end, end of file, `@./docs/dotrel.md`, `@docs/slash.md/` (as docs/slash.md), `@docs/NOTES` (no extension), and the chain docs/h1.md to docs/h4.md. Not loaded: `:`, `,`, `.`, `"`, `;`, `!`, `?` or `)` right after the path - nor the files named with the `:` or `,`, so the character is not read as part of the path; `(`, `"`, `'`, a lone backtick or a word character right before the `@`, so in `(@docs/paren.md)` each parenthesis alone is enough; double quotes around it; code span; fenced block; `@docs/folder/`; docs/h5.md and docs/h6.md (the fifth hop: the four-hop limit holds); docs/rootrel.md (no fallback to the repository root). Not probed: any other character next to a path (`*`, `[`, `]`, `>`, `|`, `-`, ...), `@~/`, an absolute path, a folder of the same name as a file.

24-settings-unknown-subkey.documented_note: Scope of this entry: the `sandbox` field allowNestedUserNamespaces, accepted since 0.28.0. The settings reference lists it from 2026-10-22 (read that day): scope "User or managed", "Claude Code ignores a `true` in a project's `.claude/settings.json` or `.claude/settings.local.json`"; sandboxing: "which a repository can't turn on", "set ... in `~/.claude/settings.json`, not the project's `.claude/settings.json`. Requires Claude Code v2.1.305 or later". A project file is therefore reported by 24-settings-scope, not as an unknown field.
24-settings-unknown-subkey.tested_note: Attempted 2026-10-21 on Claude Code 2.1.306, Linux: claude -p --model haiku --setting-sources project --no-session-persistence --strict-mcp-config --allowedTools Bash, sandbox.enabled and failIfUnavailable true, `unshare -U true` with and without the field. Not evidence either way: on that machine the sandbox does not start at all (apply-seccomp refused to write /proc/self/setgroups, for a plain `echo ok` too), so the field's effect was not observed.

tested_permissions_subkey.how: claude -p --model haiku --setting-sources project --strict-mcp-config --no-session-persistence --allowedTools Bash, a command `touch <file>` asked once per settings file: (a) permissions.deny ["Bash(touch *)"]; (b) permissions.bash.deny only; (c) permissions.bash{allow,requireApproval,deny} beside a valid permissions.deny; (d) an unknown top-level key beside a valid permissions.deny. First measured on 2.1.309 (2026-10-23).
tested_permissions_subkey.result: (a) refused. (b) the command ran, nothing on stderr. (c) refused: the unknown subkey voids its own rules, not the file or the block. (d) refused. `ask` under an unknown subkey: same mechanism, not measured. Interactive session (/doctor, startup screen): not measured.

24-settings-unknown-subkey.tested_permissions_subkey_note: WARN for an unknown subkey of `permissions` holding `deny` or `ask`; NOTICE for any other unknown subkey. Measured for `deny` only.

50-security-sandbox-weakened.documented: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sandboxing (Keep developers from widening the policy: "Each one weakens the sandbox"); https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings-reference (sandbox.enableWeakerNestedSandbox, sandbox.enableWeakerNetworkIsolation)
50-security-sandbox-weakened.documented_note: Read 2026-10-21. sandboxing lists enableWeakerNestedSandbox, enableWeakerNetworkIsolation, network.allowAllUnixSockets, network.allowLocalBinding and allowAppleEvents as keys a repository's .claude/settings.json can turn on (allowAppleEvents excepted) and says "Each one weakens the sandbox". settings-reference: enableWeakerNestedSandbox "reduces security; use it only when the outer container already provides the isolation you need", enableWeakerNetworkIsolation "reduces security by opening a potential data exfiltration path through the trust service"; the four have Scope Any file with limits on project and local settings, default false. allowAppleEvents and filesystem.disabled are Scope User or managed, so a project file is reported by 24-settings-scope instead. sandbox.allowNestedUserNamespaces is not read by this check: the settings reference (read 2026-10-22) gives it scope "User or managed" and says Claude Code ignores a `true` in a project's settings.json and settings.local.json, so 24-settings-scope reports it (catch-up audit of 0.28.0, B-00). Under an admin-required sandbox, Claude Code ignores a true in a repository's .claude/settings.json and .claude/settings.local.json for the four keys of the sandboxing table (Repository settings under an admin-required sandbox). The audit does not read managed settings; the message says so.
50-security-sandbox-weakened.tested_note: Attempted 2026-10-21 on Claude Code 2.1.306, Linux: claude -p --model haiku --setting-sources project --no-session-persistence --strict-mcp-config --allowedTools=Bash, sandbox.enabled, failIfUnavailable true and allowUnsandboxedCommands false, enableWeakerNestedSandbox false then true, command `echo SBXOK; head -c 60 /proc/1/cmdline`. Not evidence either way: both runs failed before the command ran with the same apply-seccomp error (write /proc/self/setgroups, nested userns is capability-restricted), so no key's effect was observed. The check reads only what the documentation says.

14-ondemand-file-size.documented: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory (Claude ignores the end of my subdirectory CLAUDE.md)
14-ondemand-file-size.documented_note: Read 2026-10-23. "When a subdirectory `CLAUDE.md` or a rules file that loads on demand is over a per-file size limit, Claude receives only the start of it"; the limit applies to `CLAUDE.md` and `CLAUDE.local.md` in a subdirectory (and the files they import), to rules files in a subdirectory's `.claude/rules/`, and to path-scoped rules in the project's `.claude/rules/` or in `~/.claude/rules/` (the last is outside the project and not read); 40,000 characters on a 200K context window, 200,000 on a 1M window for Claude Opus 4.6 and Claude Sonnet 4.6 and 150,000 on later models; "Before v2.1.309, Claude Code didn't apply this limit". The audit cannot see the window, so it reports the smallest limit as a NOTICE and does not count `@path` imports.
14-ondemand-file-size.tested_note: Not tested: the documented limit is not replayed against a model.

02-frontmatter-early-close.documented: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills (frontmatter that does not parse loads the skill with no fields set); no page says where the frontmatter ends
02-frontmatter-early-close.documented_note: Nothing documents the closing rule: the claim stands on the measurement. Documented only: a frontmatter that fails to parse leaves the skill loaded with empty metadata.

tested.how: claude -p --model haiku --setting-sources project --strict-mcp-config --no-session-persistence; skills, agent, rule and command with `---` in a plain value, in a quoted value, on a `----` line of a `|` block and in a YAML comment line; a hook command read from the injected message and from witness files; `claude plugin validate` on the quoted case. Measured on 2.1.309 (2026-10-23) for all of these; replayed on 2.1.317 (2026-11-03) for the skills, the hook command, the validator, the comment line and the agent only (rules and commands: 2.1.309 only).
tested.result: The frontmatter closes at the first `---` met, anywhere. A plain value is cut (`Alpha---Beta` is read `Alpha`), a hook command is cut (`touch w e---src` runs `touch w e`), a quoted value leaves an unclosed quote: `plugin validate` says the YAML failed to parse and the skill loads with empty metadata; an agent in that state was not listed (2 runs, 2.1.317). A rule losing `paths` and a hook never registered were seen on 2.1.309 only. Not measured: Windows, macOS, skills of a plugin, an agent whose YAML parses after the cut.

35-hooks-skill-event.documented: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks (Hooks in skills and agents); https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents ("All hook events are supported", for subagents only)

(b) 9 of 9 runs used the scoped name from the first call, with no difference between Haiku and Sonnet; no failed call was seen. reported: https://github.com/anthropics/claude-plugins-official/issues/6885 (a command's `argument-hint: [system] [--source <path>]` is not valid YAML; the reporter says a strict parser drops the whole command)

54-agents-md-import.documented: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory (`@path` imports in memory files, AGENTS.md included); nothing on the Codex side: the Codex AGENTS.md guide says nothing about `@` imports

24-settings-env-ignored.documented: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings-reference ("Variables Claude Code ignores in env", "When Claude Code applies env values"; read 2026-11-05)
24-settings-env-ignored.documented_note: Quoted: project and local settings "can't set variables that a checked-out repository shouldn't control"; Claude Code "drops each one, apart from a few values that turn telemetry off, and logs a warning you can see with `claude --debug`". The lists in the check are the documentation's, by name and by family (`XDG_*`, `CLAUDE_AX_*`, `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_*` with the listed suffixes). Some are ignored from every file. Version bounds are documented per group (v2.1.251, v2.1.282, v2.1.290 and others): the check does not read the Claude Code version, so on an older release a variable may still have applied. Reported as a user problem in anthropics/claude-code#107139. Id used: `24-settings-scope`.

tested.how: claude -p --model claude-haiku-5-5 --setting-sources project,local --strict-mcp-config --no-session-persistence --allowedTools Bash; a project `.claude/settings.local.json` env block holding XDG_CONFIG_HOME, CLAUDE_CODE_TMPDIR, CLAUDE_CODE_PLUGIN_CACHE_DIR and a control variable; the model ran `env | grep` on the four names; second run with --debug.
tested.result: Only the control variable reached the shell command. With --debug, one WARN line per dropped variable: "... in .claude/settings.local.json is ignored - project-scoped settings can't set this key. Set it in ~/.claude/settings.json or managed settings instead." Without --debug nothing was printed (stderr empty). One run each; three variables of the listed families, not the whole list. The user-settings side and the telemetry off values were not run.
